draft.title: A significant person in Islam
card: A significant person in a religion is someone whose life, teaching or example shaped the beliefs, law or practice of its followers. In Islam, such people are studied for their effect on the tradition.
A scholar who lived from about 767 to 820 CE. He set out how Islamic law is to be drawn from sources: the Quran, the Sunnah (the example of the Prophet Muhammad), consensus and analogy.
A wife of the Prophet Muhammad. She was a leading source of hadith, the reports of what the Prophet said and did, and she taught many students.
Both figures shaped how Muslims know and apply Islamic teaching. Al-Shafi'i did this through method in law, and Aisha through passing on knowledge of the Prophet's example.
draft.remember: Significant people shape a tradition by how they build and pass on its teaching.

a.q: Which describes al-Shafi'i's significance in Islam?
opts: He set out a method for drawing law from its sources
He was the first person to receive the Quran's message
He wrote the Quran down as a single book of law
He led the first Muslim community after the Prophet
a.why: Al-Shafi'i is significant for explaining how law is drawn from the Quran, the Sunnah and other sources. The Quran was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad, not to al-Shafi'i, so the other options describe roles he did not hold.
a.clue: Think about his work on how law is drawn from sources.

b.q: A student says Aisha shaped Islamic tradition. Which evidence best supports this?
opts: She reported and taught what the Prophet said and did
She founded a school of Islamic law named after her
She wrote a method for reasoning by analogy in law
She was the first scholar to explain the Sunnah's role
b.why: Aisha shaped tradition by passing on hadith, which record the Prophet's words and actions, and by teaching others. The method of drawing law from sources is linked to al-Shafi'i, so options about legal method or founding a law school do not fit her.
b.clue: Her influence came through passing on knowledge of the Prophet's example.

a.best: He set out a method for drawing law from its sources

b.best: She reported and taught what the Prophet said and did
